transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... it's the talking. I keep hearing people talking about me, mostly through the conference room walls at the office. Or from my phone, which is ridiculous because it happens even when the device is completely powered down. It's usually the board members or some of my senior staff, and they're always saying that I'm ruining the company. 

Which, by the way, is entirely unfair because our Q3 margins were actually up by four percent. I had to fight tooth and nail for that budget, especially with the new vendor contracts. We actually switched to this local supplier for the office coffee recently because the old one kept sending us these incredibly bitter dark roasts. I absolutely cannot stand dark roast, it completely upsets my stomach. My husband used to drink it every single morning, just filling the whole kitchen with that burnt smell, and I told him, I said, you really need to switch to a breakfast blend... um... wait, what was I... 

Right, the board members. The things they're saying through the walls, it just sounds so real. It's so perfectly clear that I actually answer them out loud. I'll just be sitting there at my desk defending my decisions to the wall before I even realize that no one else in the room heard a thing.
Have you ever had beliefs or thoughts that others don't seem to share, or that you later realized weren't accurate?

Beliefs that others don't share? No, I don't think so. I mean, obviously, as a CEO, I have a strategic vision for the company that not everyone grasps immediately. Like my VP of Marketing, Greg. He just couldn't understand why we needed to switch to a matte finish on our new packaging. I kept explaining to him that glossy just reflects the fluorescent lights in the store aisles and it makes the product look incredibly cheap. 

I was actually at the grocery store just last Tuesday looking for those little imported olives my husband likes—the ones stuffed with the almonds? And they had completely reorganized the store. They moved all the international foods right next to the dairy section, which makes absolutely no sense from a foot-traffic perspective. Plus, the dairy aisle is always freezing. I literally had to keep my coat zipped all the way up just to buy a carton of almond milk, and the cashier was moving so slowly... um, but anyway. What were we talking about? Oh, my thoughts. No, my thoughts are perfectly accurate. I don't really know what you mean by that.

Besides hearing voices through the walls or your phone, have you ever experienced any other unusual perceptions, like seeing things others don't see or believing something strongly that others don't seem to understand?

Seeing things? No, definitely not. My vision is perfectly fine. Well, I did just have to get a new prescription last month because the anti-glare coating on my old lenses started peeling off at the corners. It was so distracting during video calls. I ended up getting these new tortoiseshell frames from a boutique downtown, right next to that Italian place... oh, what's it called? Bella Vita. We had our anniversary dinner there last year, and the sea bass was just incredibly dry. My husband tried to tell the waiter, but you know how restaurants are lately, they just don't have the experienced staff to care anymore. The valet actually scratched the rear bumper of my Lexus that night, too. I was absolutely furious. I had to take it into the body shop, and they took three weeks just to match the pearl paint perfectly. It's just impossible to get good service anywhere these days... um, but wait. What were you asking about? My eyesight? No, I don't see anything that isn't there. And I don't have any strange beliefs, I just know how things actually are.
Can you sometimes feel like your thoughts are jumping all over the place, or that you're having trouble keeping your ideas organized when you speak?

Jumping all over the place? No, not at all. As a CEO, I have to be incredibly organized. I actually use a very specific color-coded system for my daily schedule. My new executive assistant, Chloe, she tried to migrate my entire calendar to this new cloud-based app last month, and I told her absolutely not. I need to see everything laid out on my desk. She's young, you know, right out of college, and she's always on her phone. I swear, that generation just cannot communicate without a screen. 

I took her out for a welcome lunch at this little bistro near the plaza, and she spent half the time taking pictures of her salad. Which, by the way, was wildly overpriced. Twenty-two dollars for some spinach and a few candied walnuts? It's ridiculous. I used to buy walnuts in bulk at the farmer's market when we lived out in the suburbs, but the squirrels would always get into the garage and chew through the bags. We had to hire this pest control guy who drove this bright yellow truck that parked right on my lawn and ruined the grass... um... wait. What did you ask me? Did you ask about the lawn? 

No, my thoughts don't jump around. I speak very clearly, I just have a lot to manage.
Have you ever had any thoughts or beliefs that others have told you are not true or seem unusual, even if you still believe they are correct?

Thoughts that people tell me aren't true? No, I don't think so. People generally agree with me, or at least they know better than to argue with the chief executive. Well, except for that interior designer we hired for the lobby renovation last quarter, Marcus. He had this completely bizarre idea that we should paint the accent walls seafoam green. Seafoam! Can you imagine? It looks exactly like a hospital from the 1980s. 

Speaking of which, when my mother was in the hospital for her hip replacement—this was a few years ago—the food they served her was absolutely atrocious. They gave her this gelatinous chicken broth that looked exactly like dishwater. I actually make my own bone broth at home now because of that. You have to simmer it for at least twenty-four hours to really extract the collagen, you know. I bought this beautiful stainless steel slow cooker specifically for it, but the power cord is ridiculously short. I had to go to the hardware store just to buy a heavy-duty extension cord so it would reach the outlet behind my kitchen island, and the teenager working in that aisle was absolutely no help at all, just staring at his phone the entire time I was trying to ask him about voltage ratings... 

Um, wait. Did you ask about the kitchen remodel? What were we talking about? No, my beliefs are perfectly normal. I don't have unusual thoughts, I just have very high standards.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or broadcasted so that others can hear them?

Put into my mind? No, of course not. My thoughts are my own, completely. I've always been a very independent thinker. That's how you get to the top, honestly. You have to trust your own instincts. Like when we were looking for a new location for our regional office, everyone—and I mean everyone on the board—wanted that glass high-rise downtown. But I knew the traffic patterns there were a nightmare. 

I actually read this fascinating article on urban planning and traffic flow while I was waiting at the dentist last week. Dr. Evans, he's been my dentist for fifteen years, but his waiting room is freezing. I always have to bring that cashmere wrap I bought in Aspen. We took a ski trip there last winter, and the snow was practically non-existent. It was so disappointing. My husband rented these incredibly expensive skis, and he ended up just sitting in the lodge drinking hot toddies the whole time. Which reminds me, I need to pick up some cinnamon sticks before the holidays, the good kind from that spice market across town. The parking there is terrible, though, you always have to parallel park on this steep hill, and the last time I did that, the car behind me bumped my trailer hitch... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Did you ask about the office move? 

No, my thoughts are mine. Nobody is putting them there or taking them out, that's absurd. I just have a very active mind.
Do you ever feel like people are talking about you or plotting against you, even when there's no clear reason for it?

Plotting against me? No, I don't think so. I mean, in business you always have competitors trying to outmaneuver you, but that's just standard market dynamics, not some personal plot. Like last year, this rival firm tried to undercut our pricing right before the annual expo in Chicago. 

Chicago is incredibly windy, by the way, they really aren't exaggerating about that. I wore this gorgeous vintage silk scarf that my husband bought me in Milan, and it nearly blew right off my neck when we were walking out of the hotel. We stayed at The Drake, which is normally lovely, but their elevators were moving at a glacial pace that weekend. I spent half my morning just standing in the lobby, staring at this massive floral centerpiece they had on the main table. 

I really don't know who their florist is, but they used these enormous stargazer lilies, and I absolutely cannot stand the smell of lilies. They always remind me of funerals. When my great-aunt Martha passed away, the church was just overflowing with them. She actually left me her antique mahogany credenza in her will, which is sitting in my formal dining room right now, but the wood is starting to warp because the humidity in our house is completely unregulated. I keep calling the HVAC company to come fix the smart thermostat, but the technician just tinkers with the wiring for ten minutes and charges me a fortune for the service call... 

Um, wait. What were you asking me? Did you ask about the air conditioning? 

No, nobody is talking about me or plotting anything. I'm the chief executive, people respect my authority.
Do you ever feel that certain events, messages, or actions by others are specifically directed at you, even if they don’t seem to be connected?

Directed at me? Like hidden messages or something? No, not at all. If someone wants to tell me something, they send an email or schedule a meeting. I certainly don't have time for subliminal nonsense. 

Speaking of emails, though, my inbox was an absolute disaster this morning because the IT department decided to push a massive software update over the weekend without my explicit approval. The new interface is this glaring, obnoxious shade of yellow. Yellow! It gives me an immediate headache just looking at the screen. I actually had to take an aspirin before my nine o'clock conference call. I only buy the name-brand aspirin, by the way, the generic ones always leave this awful chalky taste in the back of your throat. 

I keep a little bottle in my handbag—it's this beautiful leather tote I picked up on a business trip to Florence last spring. The leather craftsmanship in Italy is just unparalleled, you really can't find anything like it stateside. While we were there, we ate at this tiny trattoria right off the main piazza, and the pasta was entirely handmade. You can really taste the difference when they use fresh egg yolks. I tried making fresh pasta at home once after that trip, but the flour got absolutely everywhere, it was embedded in the grout of my kitchen floor for weeks. The cleaning service we use is usually very thorough, but they completely ignored the grout that week. I had to leave a very stern note for the head housekeeper, and honestly, good help is just so hard to find these days... 

Um, wait. I'm sorry, what was the question? Were we talking about the new office software? 

No, I don't think random events are directed at me. If someone has something to say to the chief executive, they say it directly.
Have you ever felt that things people do or say, even if not directly to you, were secretly about you or meant to harm or communicate something to you specifically?

Secretly about me? No, I don't think so. I mean, people talk, obviously, but I don't assume every little conversation is a coded message meant for me. I'm busy enough without trying to decipher office gossip. Honestly, if people have time to whisper in corners, they clearly don't have enough on their plates. 

I was just saying that to my assistant, David, the other day. He was lingering by the water cooler for entirely too long. We just had that new filtration system installed, the one that dispenses sparkling water too. It's supposed to be better for the environment than all those plastic bottles, but the carbonation level is completely inconsistent. Sometimes it's barely fizzy, and other times it's like a geyser. It actually sprayed all over my silk blouse right before a luncheon with the board of directors. 

I had to rush home to change, which was a nightmare because they're doing construction on the interstate again. They've been working on that same stretch of highway for three years, and I swear, the potholes are only getting worse. I hit one so hard last month it completely ruined the alignment on my Mercedes. The dealership took three days to fix it, and they gave me this awful, tiny little loaner car that smelled faintly of wet dog. I don't even own a dog. I'm allergic to dander, it makes my eyes water terribly. I tried taking those over-the-counter antihistamines, but they just make me incredibly drowsy, and I can't afford to be falling asleep during quarterly reviews...

Wait, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Something about David at the water cooler?

No, I don't think people are secretly trying to communicate with me or harm me. If they have an issue, they know my door is open, provided they schedule it with my assistant first.

Do you ever feel that random events, like things you see on TV, in the news, or things people say in public, are specifically related to you or have a special meaning for you, even if they don’t seem connected to others?

No, I don't think so. I mean, the news is just the news, right? It's mostly about the economy or whatever crisis is happening overseas. I don't watch much TV anyway, honestly, I don't have the time. My husband watches those ridiculous reality shows about real estate agents in Los Angeles, which I find completely baffling. 

Why anyone would pay ten million dollars for a house that's practically hanging off a cliff in an earthquake zone is beyond me. We looked at real estate in California once, years ago, before I got the promotion to chief executive. The agent showed us this mid-century modern place with floor-to-ceiling windows, which sounds nice, but think about the heating bill. And the glass! You'd have to hire someone just to wash the windows full-time. We had a window washer at the office who used this squeegee that left terrible streaks on the glass in my corner office. I finally had to tell building management to switch vendors because it looked incredibly unprofessional when I had clients in for meetings. 

The new vendor is much better, though they use this cleaning solution that smells strongly of ammonia. It reminds me of the time I tried to clean my grandmother's old silver tea set. I used the wrong polish and it tarnished the whole thing. It was a tragedy, really, because it was a wedding gift to her from my grandfather. They got married in the winter, and she always said the snow was so deep they almost couldn't get to the church. I hate the snow, it ruins all my good leather shoes. I have this pair of Italian pumps...

Wait, I'm sorry. What were we talking about? The window washers? 

No, I don't think the news or TV shows are about me. I'm just a normal executive trying to run a company.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or broadcasted so that others can hear them?

Thoughts put into my mind? Like someone else is controlling them? Or broadcasting them? No, absolutely not. My thoughts are my own. I mean, if someone were broadcasting my thoughts, they'd probably be pretty bored, honestly. It's mostly just quarterly projections and supply chain logistics right now. 

Speaking of the supply chain, the shipping delays we've been dealing with lately are completely out of control. We source a lot of our raw materials from overseas, and the bottleneck at the ports is a nightmare. I was on a call with our logistics director for three hours yesterday, and he was trying to explain the container shortage. Apparently, there are thousands of empty shipping containers just sitting in the wrong ports. It's incredibly inefficient. I hate inefficiency. It's like when you go to the grocery store and they only have one checkout lane open, but there are five employees just standing around near the self-checkout staring at their phones. 

I actually saw that happen last Tuesday when I ran in to grab a bottle of wine for a dinner party. I was hosting a few of the senior VP's, and I wanted to serve this beautiful Cabernet I discovered on a trip to Napa Valley. The vineyards out there are stunning, especially in the early autumn when the leaves are just starting to turn. We stayed at this lovely boutique hotel that had a spa, and I got a hot stone massage that completely melted the tension in my shoulders. I really carry all my stress in my shoulders. My chiropractor says it's from hunching over my laptop too much. He recommended this ergonomic chair, but it's incredibly ugly. It looks like some sort of medieval torture device, all black mesh and weird lumbar supports. I refuse to put something that hideous in my office. My office was professionally decorated, you know. I chose a very calming palette of slate gray and navy blue...

Wait, I'm sorry, I completely lost my train of thought again. What was the question? Something about the supply chain?

No, no one is putting thoughts in my head or taking them out. That sounds like something out of a science fiction movie. My mind is entirely my own business.

No, I don't think so. I mean, my thoughts are my own. Nobody's putting them there or broadcasting them or whatever. If they were, I think they'd be pretty bored, to be honest. It's mostly just... well, right now it's mostly about the quarterly projections and the supply chain logistics.

I chose a very calming palette of slate gray and navy blue...

No, no one is putting thoughts in my head or taking them out. That sounds like something out of a science fiction movie. My mind is entirely my own business.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or broadcasted so that others can hear them?

Didn't you just ask me that? I feel like we literally just went over this. No, nobody is broadcasting my thoughts or putting them in my head. I'm pretty sure I just said that. 

It feels a bit like I'm back in one of our executive committee meetings, honestly. Everyone just repeating the exact same points over and over because they weren't listening the first time. My former assistant, David, was terrible about that. I'd tell him exactly how I wanted the quarterly reports bound—spiral, clear cover, navy back—and he'd ask me the same question again five minutes later. I finally had to let him go. 

Finding good help right now is just impossible. The talent pool is completely dry. We put out a listing for an entry-level analyst and got a hundred resumes from people who didn't even know how to use basic spreadsheet functions. I don't know what they teach in college these days. When I was taking classes, we actually had to memorize formulas. I didn't finish my degree, obviously, because I started my first business when I was twenty-two and the opportunity was just too good to pass up, but at least I learned the basics. My niece is in college right now, studying something completely unmarketable, like 17th-century French poetry or something. She wants to study abroad in Paris next spring. Paris is lovely in the spring, but the traffic around the Arc de Triomphe is absolutely terrifying. I took a cab there once and I swear the driver closed his eyes when he merged into the roundabout. I spilled my coffee all over my trench coat. It was a classic Burberry, too, the camel color, and the dry cleaner could never quite get the stain out...

Wait, what were we just talking about? Did you ask about David? 

Oh, right, my thoughts. Yes, like I just said, they are mine. Nobody is taking them or broadcasting them anywhere.
Have you ever felt that things people do or say, even when they aren’t directed at you, were actually meant for you or carried a special message intended just for you?

Special messages? Like hidden meanings or something? No, not at all. People in my line of work are usually pretty blunt. If they have something to say to me, they just send an email or bring it up in a board meeting. Though honestly, nobody reads emails properly anymore anyway. 

It's incredible how poor communication has gotten in the corporate world. We just launched this massive internal communications initiative last quarter, spent an absolute fortune on these consultants from Boston. They brought in these huge, glossy posters to put up in all the regional offices. I told them the font was completely wrong, though. They used Helvetica. I despise Helvetica. It's so terribly overused. It reminds me of the signage at the airport. I was at JFK last month flying out to a conference in Chicago, and the signage was just abysmal. I almost missed my flight because the terminal numbers were completely obscured by this ridiculous construction project they're doing. 

And the construction in Chicago is even worse, if you can believe it! They've been working on the exact same stretch of highway for what feels like a decade. My Uber driver hit a pothole so hard I thought the axle was going to snap right in half. It was a nice car, too, one of those big black Suburbans. I've actually been thinking about upgrading my own vehicle lately. The lease on my Mercedes is up in three months, and I kind of want an SUV. Something with more trunk space for golf clubs. I don't even golf that much, but I joined this exclusive country club last year mostly for the networking. The food there is incredibly disappointing, though. They overcook the salmon every single time, it's like eating a dry sponge, and the hollandaise sauce always separates...

Wait... why was I talking about salmon? I completely lost my place. What were you asking me? Something about my emails? 

Oh, right. No, no secret messages or anything meant just for me. Just normal, everyday conversations.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being controlled by an outside force, like someone else is putting thoughts into your mind or pulling them out?

Are you reading off a checklist or something? Because I swear we've covered this exact thing twice already. No, nobody is controlling my thoughts or pulling them out. I am completely in control of my own mind. 

Honestly, the only thing being controlled by an outside force in my life right now is my house, and it's driving me absolutely insane. I had this high-end, fully automated smart home system installed last month. The contractor promised it would streamline my routine, but it's completely malfunctioning. The thermostat drops to sixty degrees at two in the morning for absolutely no reason. I wake up freezing, shivering under my duvet. It's a custom goose-down duvet I ordered from this little boutique in Switzerland when I was there for an economic summit. Switzerland is gorgeous, but the prices are just extortionate. I bought a cup of coffee in Zurich that cost me the equivalent of fifteen dollars, and it wasn't even a good roast. It was incredibly acidic. I can't stand acidic coffee, it gives me terrible heartburn. My doctor told me I need to cut back on caffeine entirely, but how on earth do you run a company on chamomile tea? It's a ridiculous suggestion. He also told me to eat more leafy greens, so I hired a private chef to meal-prep for me, but she keeps making these raw kale salads that taste like literal dirt. I don't care how many candied walnuts or goat cheese crumbles you put on it, kale is just a weed. It's like chewing on tree bark. I had a Golden Retriever growing up that used to chew on tree bark in the backyard, and my mother would get so furious because he'd track mud all over the white carpets...

Wait, what did you ask me? Why am I talking about my mother's carpets? Did you ask about my house? 

Oh, the mind control thing. Right. No. Like I just said, I'm the one in control. Always.

Have you ever felt that events, actions, or things you see or hear in the world around you—like something on TV, in a book, or something someone said in public—were secretly about you or meant something special just for you?

Are you actually listening to my answers, or are you just reading down a list of synonyms? Because you literally just asked me about secret messages like five minutes ago. No, the TV is not talking to me. Books are not secretly about me. 

I barely even have time to watch television anyway. The only thing I ever have on is Bloomberg in my office, just to keep an eye on the markets. The volatility this quarter is just staggering. I pulled half my personal portfolio out of tech last week because the valuations are completely divorced from reality. I was at this charity gala on Saturday, sitting next to the founder of some new app startup, and the kid couldn't even articulate his own revenue model to me. He was wearing this absolutely hideous velvet tuxedo jacket, too. Who on earth wears velvet in May? It was completely stifling in that ballroom. The venue's air conditioning was barely functioning, and they had these massive, over-the-top floral centerpieces that completely blocked everyone's view of the podium. Stargazer lilies, I think. I'm actually terribly allergic to lilies. My eyes were watering the entire night, and I'm pretty sure I ruined my makeup. It was a brand new foundation, too, cost an absolute fortune, but the sales associate swore it would last through high humidity. She was working at the cosmetics counter at Neiman Marcus, and honestly, the customer service there has really gone downhill since the pandemic. You used to be able to get a proper consultation, but now they just ring you up and shove the bag at you...

Wait, why am I telling you about my makeup? What did you just ask me? Something about the gala?

Oh, right. The TV and the books. No. Like I keep telling you, I don't think the news or random things in public are secretly about me. Can we please move on to a different topic now?
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or broadcasted so that others can hear them?

Are you... are you joking? I feel like I'm taking crazy pills here. You literally asked me this exact same question—about thoughts being put in or taken out of my mind—just a few minutes ago! Are you even listening to me, or are you just reading off a broken teleprompter? No, my thoughts are not being broadcasted. Nobody is putting them there. I am a CEO, for heaven's sake, my thoughts are my own and they are highly confidential. 

Confidentiality is actually a massive issue for us right now. We had a potential data breach last week that had my entire legal team working through the weekend. It turned out to be a false alarm, just some low-level IT guy who misconfigured a firewall, but the sheer panic it caused was unbelievable. I had to fire him on Monday. I hate firing people on Mondays, it sets a terrible tone for the entire week, but honestly, incompetence is the one thing I absolutely will not tolerate. My father was the exact same way. He ran a manufacturing plant in Ohio and he would fire people on the spot if they were late twice in one month. He was a very strict man, always wore these impeccably pressed suits, even on the weekends. He used to take his suits to this little Italian tailor downtown who charged an arm and a leg, but the craftsmanship was stunning. You just don't see that kind of tailoring anymore, especially with all these fast-fashion brands taking over. I bought a blazer from one of those trendy online boutiques once just to see what the fuss was about, and the stitching started unraveling after one dry clean. The dry cleaner I use now is fantastic, though. They use this eco-friendly solvent that doesn't leave that horrible chemical smell on your clothes. I can't stand strong chemical smells, they give me the worst migraines. I had a migraine so bad last month I had to cancel my dinner reservations at Le Bernardin, and it takes months to get a table there...

Wait, why am I talking about my dry cleaner? I'm sorry, I'm just so frustrated that you keep repeating yourself. What was the question again? Something about my thoughts? 

Right. No. No one is broadcasting my thoughts or putting them in my head. Can we please move on to something else before you ask me this a fourth time?
Have you ever felt that things people do or say—like something on TV, in a book, or in public—were secretly about you or meant something special for you, even if they didn’t seem connected to others?

Are you literally just reading the same page over and over? Because I feel like I am losing my mind here. You just asked me about the TV and the books and the secret messages! I already told you no! Nothing on television or in public is secretly about me. I do not have the time to sit around decoding special meanings from a broadcast. 

Do you have any idea how much my time is worth? Because sitting here listening to you repeat yourself is costing me an absolute fortune. It honestly reminds me of this management consulting firm I hired last fall. Absolute waste of space. I paid them over half a million dollars to audit our supply chain, and they literally just handed me a fifty-page PowerPoint of things my own COO had already told me. And the formatting was atrocious. They used this hideous neon orange for all the bar graphs. It looked like a cheap Halloween decoration. I actually take Halloween very seriously, I host a massive masquerade at my estate every year. Last year, I hired this caterer who specialized in molecular gastronomy, and they made these little edible smoke bubbles that tasted like black cherry. It was visually stunning, but honestly, the smoke alarm went off in the west wing because of it. The fire department showed up, and the fire chief tracked mud all over the imported Spanish tile in my foyer. Do you know how hard it is to source authentic terracotta from Andalusia right now? The shipping delays are just a nightmare. I had a shipment of patio furniture stuck at the Port of Los Angeles for six months...

Wait, what? Why am I talking about the Port of LA? Did you ask me about my patio furniture? 

Ugh, no, you asked that ridiculous TV question again. For the absolute last time, no. Nobody is sending me special messages. Now please, ask me something new or I am walking out of here.

Have you ever felt that random events, like something you saw on TV or in the news, or something someone said in public, was secretly connected to you or had a special meaning just for you, even if it didn’t seem related to others?

Is this a joke? Is there a hidden camera in here? Because I am genuinely looking around the room for a camera right now. You have asked me this exact same thing about the TV and the news four times! No! The answer is still no! 

Honestly, if this is some kind of prank, it's not funny. It reminds me of those awful reality shows. I actually met one of those reality TV producers at a charity gala in Miami a few years ago. He was pitching me this completely absurd concept about wealthy female executives living on a yacht. As if I have time to live on a yacht. I don't even like boats. The last time I was on a yacht was off the Amalfi coast, and the water was so choppy I spilled a glass of vintage Dom Pérignon all over my white silk trousers. Silk is an absolute nightmare to clean, by the way. You can't just spot-treat it, it leaves a massive water ring. I had to have my assistant fly the pants back to New York to my specialist cleaner. 

My assistant is usually very good about handling those little crises, but she’s been so distracted lately because she’s planning her wedding. She’s insisting on this destination wedding in Tuscany, which is just so incredibly cliché. Everyone does Tuscany. And she actually expects me to give her two weeks of paid leave for it right in the middle of our Q3 earnings reports. I told her she needs to reschedule, but this younger generation just has zero work ethic. They want all the perks without putting in the hours. When I started my first company, I was literally sleeping under my desk. I didn't even finish college because I was too busy building a business, and now I have people with Master's degrees asking me for "mental health days" because they feel overwhelmed by their email inbox. It's pathetic, really. You have to be ruthless if you want to survive in this market...
